root_cause.text: A race in `bpf_sk_storage`’s RCU traversal lets readers in `bpf_sk_storage_clone()` and diag code dereference `SDATA(selem)->smap` after `bpf_selem_unlink_nofail()` has already cleared that pointer to NULL while the element is still on the hlist.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says `bpf_selem_unlink_nofail()` “sets SDATA(selem)->smap to NULL before removing the selem from the storage hlist,” and the patch fixes the crash by adding `if (!smap)` checks in `bpf_sk_storage_clone()` and `bpf_sk_storage_diag_put_all()`, plus refactoring `diag_get()` to take a validated `smap` parameter instead of reading `sdata->smap` internally.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null check in bpf_sk_storage_clone() to avoid dereferencing a missing storage map during cloning.
intent_record.what: In `bpf_sk_storage_clone()`, the conditional was changed from `if (!(smap->map.map_flags & BPF_F_CLONE))` to `if (!smap || !(smap->map.map_flags & BPF_F_CLONE))`, adding a null check for `smap` before dereferencing it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents a possible null pointer dereference if `rcu_dereference(SDATA(selem)->smap)` returns `NULL`; when `smap` is absent, the code now skips cloning that storage entry instead of accessing `smap->map` and potentially crashing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the local storage map into `diag_get` explicitly instead of declaring it locally.
intent_record.what: The function `diag_get` was changed to take an explicit `struct bpf_local_storage_map *smap` parameter, and the local declaration of `smap` inside the function was removed.
intent_record.how: Callers now supply the storage map directly to `diag_get` instead of the function deriving or declaring it locally, which changes the function interface but not the visible logic in the shown body. This enables the function to use the correct map context passed in from the caller.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the redundant RCU dereference assignment in `diag_get()` while continuing to report the storage map ID.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the local assignment `smap = rcu_dereference(sdata->smap);` from `diag_get()`, leaving the subsequent use of `smap->map.id` unchanged.
intent_record.how: As shown, the function no longer performs an explicit RCU dereference before reading `smap->map.id`, which changes how the pointer is obtained at runtime; this can affect synchronization and the safety of accessing the storage map reference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip storage entries with a missing map pointer and pass the map into diag_get() to avoid invalid processing in BPF sk storage diagnostics.
intent_record.what: In the RCU list walk inside bpf_sk_storage_diag_put_all(), the code now checks whether smap is NULL and skips the entry if so. The call to diag_get() was also changed from passing only SDATA(selem) and skb to passing smap, SDATA(selem), and skb. As a result, the function now uses the retrieved map pointer when computing diagnostic data and avoids dereferencing or operating on a missing map pointer.
intent_record.how: At runtime, entries whose storage map pointer has become unavailable are ignored instead of being processed, preventing invalid access and keeping the diagnostic size calculation and payload generation consistent with only valid storage entries. The updated diag_get() signature ensures the helper has the map context it needs to emit correct diagnostic information.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the current storage map into `diag_get()` so per-map diagnostic sizing and error handling work correctly.
intent_record.what: The call in the conditional was changed from `diag_get(sdata, skb)` to `diag_get((struct bpf_local_storage_map *)diag->maps[i], sdata, skb)`, adding the current map element as an explicit first argument and casting it to `struct bpf_local_storage_map *`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the diagnostic helper now receives the specific storage map being processed, rather than being called without that context. This lets the size/error accounting logic operate with the correct per-map information when iterating over `diag->maps[i]`, which can prevent incorrect diagnostics or sizing behavior.

consistency_review.core_intent: Update BPF sk storage diagnostics to pass the current storage map into diag_get() and handle missing map pointers safely.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the reported race by adding a NULL check in bpf_sk_storage_clone() before dereferencing SDATA(selem)->smap, which matches the root cause of readers accessing a pointer that may already have been cleared.
The change is a minor refactor to pass the local storage map into diag_get explicitly. It does not address the RCU race or the NULL dereference of SDATA(selem)->smap in bpf_sk_storage traversal.

The change is in the same diagnostic code path involved in the race: it adjusts how `diag_get()` accesses the storage map ID under RCU. Since the root cause is an unsafe dereference of `SDATA(selem)->smap` after it may have been cleared to NULL, a fix in `diag_get()` for that access pattern is directly related.

The root cause is a NULL/dangling map-pointer race in bpf_sk_storage readers. This group directly changes BPF sk storage diagnostics to pass the current map into diag_get() and skip entries with missing map pointers, which is a safety fix for the same dereference issue.

candidates.rationale: This dereferences the storage-map pointer that can be cleared to NULL by bpf_selem_unlink_nofail() while the selem is still reachable in the hlist, creating the race described in the root cause.
In the diagnostics traversal, this read of SDATA(selem)->smap can race with unlink clearing the pointer to NULL, and the next line immediately dereferences smap->map.value_size, triggering the bug.
The diagnostic helper also dereferences the storage-map pointer under RCU; if the pointer has been cleared to NULL before this read, later use of smap->map.id becomes invalid.

vuln_statements.explanation: This RCU read races with bpf_selem_unlink_nofail() clearing SDATA(selem)->smap to NULL while the selem remains on the hlist. A reader can then dereference a missing storage-map pointer during clone/diagnostic traversal.
This diagnostic-path RCU dereference can observe sdata->smap after it has been cleared to NULL by unlink, leading to invalid later use of the storage map pointer.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable RCU traversal pattern. In both dump paths, readers walk the hlist under RCU and dereference the storage map pointer from each element: `hlist_for_each_entry_rcu(selem, &sk_storage->list, snode) { smap = rcu_dereference(SDATA(selem)->smap); ... }` and later `sdata = __sk_storage_lookup(...)` followed by `diag_get(sdata, skb)`, where `diag_get()` does `smap = rcu_dereference(sdata->smap);`. The root cause says readers can dereference `SDATA(selem)->smap` after `bpf_selem_unlink_nofail()` has already cleared that pointer to NULL while the element is still on the hlist. This commit version has no NULL check or other protection before using `smap->map.value_size`, `smap->map.id`, or passing `sdata` into `diag_get()`. So the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present in this code.
